items.passage: Phreatomagmatic eruptions occur when rising magma encounters groundwater or surface water, causing the water to flash to steam and fragmenting the magma into fine ash. The resulting tephra has characteristic blocky, low-vesicularity shards that distinguish it from purely magmatic ejecta. These eruptions are common at maar volcanoes and during the early phases of submarine eruptions, where the explosive interaction between molten rock and water produces base surges that travel along the ground at high velocity.

items.passage: The Diels-Alder reaction is a [4+2] cycloaddition between a conjugated diene and a dienophile, producing a six-membered ring with up to four new stereocenters. The reaction proceeds through a concerted, suprafacial transition state and is highly stereospecific: cis-dienophiles yield cis-substituted cyclohexenes. Electron-withdrawing groups on the dienophile dramatically accelerate the reaction by lowering the LUMO energy and improving frontier orbital overlap with the diene HOMO.

items.passage: Hydrothermal vent communities at mid-ocean ridges depend on chemosynthetic bacteria that oxidize hydrogen sulfide rather than relying on photosynthesis. Tube worms in the genus Riftia harbor these bacteria as symbionts in a specialized organ called the trophosome. The vents themselves form when seawater percolates into the oceanic crust, gets heated by underlying magma, and is expelled with dissolved minerals at temperatures exceeding 350°C, producing the characteristic black smokers.

items.passage: The Chandrasekhar limit defines the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf star, approximately 1.4 solar masses. Beyond this limit, electron degeneracy pressure cannot counteract gravitational collapse, leading to either neutron star formation or a Type Ia supernova depending on composition. The exact value depends on the mean molecular weight per electron, with hydrogen-rich stars yielding slightly higher limits than carbon-oxygen white dwarfs typical of the late stages of low-mass stellar evolution.

items.passage: Vowel harmony is a phonological process in which vowels within a word are required to share certain features, such as backness or roundness. Turkish exhibits both backness and rounding harmony, with suffix vowels assimilating to the features of the stem vowel. The phenomenon is captured in autosegmental phonology by representing harmonic features on a separate tier from the segmental skeleton, with spreading rules determining how features propagate across the word domain.

items.passage: Plate tectonics describes the motion of rigid lithospheric plates over the underlying asthenosphere. Convergent boundaries form subduction zones where oceanic crust descends into the mantle, producing volcanic arcs and deep ocean trenches. Divergent boundaries occur at mid-ocean ridges where new crust is created by upwelling magma. Transform boundaries, like the San Andreas Fault, accommodate horizontal slip between plates without creating or destroying crust, and produce shallow earthquakes when accumulated strain exceeds frictional resistance.

items.passage: We compared the geometry of activation patterns across model layers and brain regions, asking whether two stimuli that produce similar activations in the model also produce similar activations in cortex. For each layer, we extracted the patterns evoked by 96 images, computed all pairwise dissimilarities using one minus the Pearson correlation, and tested whether the resulting structure aligned with that measured in human inferotemporal cortex via functional MRI.

items.passage: For each three-dimensional voxel in early visual cortex, we fit a linear weighting of features extracted from a deep convolutional network, then evaluated how well the weighted combination predicted held-out responses to natural images. The model with the highest cross-validated correlation in each voxel reflects an estimate of which image features that voxel is most sensitive to.

items.passage: Each cortical layer computes the difference between top-down predictions arriving from higher-order areas and bottom-up sensory input, sending only the unexplained residual onward to the next stage of processing. Under this view, what propagates up the cortical hierarchy is not raw sensory data but mismatch — the parts of the input that the brain's internal model failed to anticipate.

items.passage: We trained a generative model that learned to vary the orientation of a rendered object independently of its lighting, such that traversing one latent dimension changed only the orientation while leaving illumination unchanged, and vice versa. The trained latent factors thus aligned with the underlying generative factors of the data without explicit supervision on those factors.
